0300_video_deletion_retirement.schema.js.title: Video execution retirement deletion guards
0300_video_deletion_retirement.schema.js.$comment: Project and Dataset deletion require durable retirement proof for every in-scope video execution. Legacy scopes without proof fail closed and require separate recovery; absence of a canonical Job is not retirement proof.

functions.semantics: Reject NULL arrays and NULL array elements with 22023. Deduplicate and lock canonical Video Jobs by UUID with FOR UPDATE NOWAIT, then execution rows by UUID, then journals by UUID. Include already-orphaned journals whose task or project matches. Existing execution permits deletion only with a same-run retired journal and a terminal or missing canonical Job; no lease-expiry requirement is added, and clearance never substitutes for that proof. Without execution or journal, a present canonical Job must have started_at NULL and a known queued/cancelled/terminal-history status; any started legacy Job blocks even when its status is terminal. A missing canonical Job with neither journal nor clearance fails closed. After every target passes, insert an immutable clearance only for currently present qualifying never-started Jobs, inside the caller transaction, so a later scope-only orphan remains provably safe. Empty scope succeeds. No Tasks/Annotations reads or writes, retirement mutation, or transaction ownership are added.

Caller already holds Project FOR UPDATE. Lock Project TaskBatches, Tasks, then every Annotation that project deletion will cascade, all UUID-ordered FOR UPDATE NOWAIT. Collect canonical Video Job IDs from selected Tasks/Annotations, source sidecars for selected Annotations, and matching retained scopes whose canonical Job is absent, then call the Jobs guard with Task IDs and Project ID. Return the guard result without modifying owner data.

Caller has already locked Dataset/Project/association, locked Dataset unlink scope, and passed Learning/Labeling retention guards. Use the exact _dataset_unlink_task_snapshot, then lock its Annotations by UUID FOR UPDATE NOWAIT. Collect canonical Jobs and source sidecars; include orphan retained scopes matching Project and selected Task IDs or Dataset item IDs from dataset_item_references, comparing the stored item UUID text without casting it. Call the Jobs guard with Project NULL. No deletion or retirement mutation is performed.

Preserves the frozen project deletion behavior and adds the Labeling video retirement guard after the existing Learning retention guard, before any owner mutation. The stable blocker remains video_execution_not_retired.

private_tables.semantics: Private Jobs-owned evidence that a canonical Job was present, never started, and had no execution or journal when its deletion was admitted. The caller's transaction commits or rolls back the evidence together with the deletion. Rows are immutable, survive canonical Job cascades, and never substitute for same-run retired-journal proof when an execution exists. PUBLIC has no table privileges. Downgrade is refused with SQLSTATE 55000 while any evidence remains.

0312_video_tracker_input_retention.schem.title: Jobs-owned execution retention for accepted video tracker inputs

functions.semantics: Return only the accepted input identity, canonical tracker Job identity, and whether the Jobs execution still retains the input. Lock in canonical Job -> execution -> journal order. A current execution is safe only when its current-run journal is both writer-terminal and retired. Started legacy Jobs, execution rows without journals, stale journals that do not match the current run, journal-only orphans, and missing Jobs without never-started clearance retain the input. A never-started Job or cleared missing Job may follow existing Labeling retention rules. When Labeling scope is absent, recover only the ready accepted input identity through the existing Assets facts capability; malformed, unavailable, nonready, or contended facts fail closed.

Preserve checkpoint journal retention, annotation pins, queued/running retention, and existing pending-review grace. Consult Jobs before allowing ordinary expiration. If the narrow Jobs fact is unavailable or malformed, return an invalid response so the Assets sweeper skips the input. No foreign-table privilege or retirement/status mutation is introduced.

Reuse the 0312 fact contract. A Job without execution or journal releases execution retention only when it is unstarted and its status is in the explicit 0300 never-started-safe set. A current execution releases only with a same-run writer-terminal retired journal and a canonical Job that is absent or in the 0300 terminal set. Unknown, running, and NULL statuses fail closed.

Call the existing Labeling retention projection only for a current tracker source Blob still named by its immutable accepted plan, or a current frame Blob still named by its immutable frame record. A referenced or unprovable current root is deferred by one claim lease and scanning continues through the bounded page. Known superseded attempt prefixes remain collectible while the Job is live. Manifest-owned garbage keeps its prior path. Unmapped video tombstones fail closed and remain backlog.

0379_operator_item_locator.schema.json.title: aap_assets_v1.publish_operator_item_original

owner_lifecycle.allocation: Allocation is independent and FK-free: dataset_id is an opaque scope, so a caller may allocate before its Dataset is published. Publication and item/scene binding validate the business scope in the caller's unit of work. Allocation never claims.
owner_lifecycle.claim: open_operator_storage_operation(uuid) atomically acquires the write permit and claims an allocated creation (status preparing, operation_id, claimed_at); for an already verified creation it issues a distinct creation-bound read permit and leaves the creation untouched. Reply carries operation_id and mode write|read. There is no separate claim capability.
owner_lifecycle.staging: origin=direct persists the caller-reserved staging locator (staging_bucket, staging_key) plus the caller's observed etag/version_id in source; the staging bucket is independently proven from the validated import binding. staging_ref stays NULL, which the staging-ref constraint explicitly allows. A different staging key for the same authority never silently retargets.
owner_lifecycle.mode: A connection-backed datasets binding always forces mode write; only the legacy platform binding may adopt an existing source key.
owner_lifecycle.prepared: Prepared evidence is frozen only when it matches the reserved bucket/object_key and the bounded byte budget.
owner_lifecycle.writing: The writing transition atomically creates the Main storage_usage_mutations intent (producer managed_original_creation, purpose managed_original, kind create, state pending, physical_outcome unknown) with Main's exact idempotency and scope recipes.
owner_lifecycle.verified: Verification requires explicit physical_settled=true and readback equal to the frozen sha256/md5/size and the written receipt etag/version_id; it settles only this creation's write permit and finalizes the accounting intent (confirmed only with a version-pinned current-head match, otherwise unknown).
owner_lifecycle.failure: Failures carry physical_settled and physical_outcome not_written|written|unknown. A proven-drained failure settles only the matching permit and finalizes accounting (delta 0 only for not_written); an unknown drain keeps both the permit and the pending accounting window.
owner_lifecycle.close: close_operator_storage_operation(creation_id, operation_id, physical_settled) settles only a creation-bound read permit; missing/foreign permits and write permits are rejected, and an unsettled close returns operation_unsettled while retaining the permit.
owner_lifecycle.accounting: No compensating trigger exists: the native owner writes and finishes storage_usage_mutations exactly as Main's _change(record_mutation=True)/accounting does. No table or sequence privilege is granted to consumers.
